findings.title: Unpolyfilled Array/String .at(-1) crashes on Safari < 15.4 while build target floor is safari14
findings.description: wikilinks.ts:146 (`return parts.at(-1) ?? fallbackLabel;`) and NotePage.tsx:333 (`matchHeading.split(" > ").at(-1) ?? matchHeading`) call Array.prototype.at / String.prototype.at. Vite has no `build.target` in vite.config.ts, so it uses the default 'modules' preset whose baseline is [es2020, edge88, firefox78, chrome87, safari14]. esbuild does NOT down-level runtime methods like `.at()` (only syntax), so the code ships verbatim. `.at()` first shipped in Safari/iOS 15.4 (March 2022).
findings.why: On Safari/iOS 14.x-15.3 `arr.at` is undefined, so the call throws `TypeError: parts.at is not a function`. wikilinks.ts runs while rendering wikilink labels in note bodies (very common path), so the whole note render throws; NotePage.tsx:333 breaks heading-anchored navigation. This is an engine-version gap between the declared build floor (safari14) and an API that needs 15.4.
findings.fixSketch: Either set `build.target` to a floor that guarantees `.at` (safari15.4+) and document it, or avoid `.at(-1)`: use `parts[parts.length - 1]`. Same for NotePage.tsx:333.

findings.title: Search dialog input relies on React autoFocus; iOS WebKit will not raise the soft keyboard
findings.description: The search field uses `autoFocus` (line 159) and is also programmatically focused via `inputRef.current?.focus()` from keyboard navigation (line 205). React applies `autoFocus` during commit (a microtask after the click that opened the dialog), and the ArrowUp focus() call is inside a keydown handler on the list, not on the input.
findings.why: WebKit on iOS only presents the on-screen keyboard when `.focus()` executes synchronously inside a user-gesture (touch/click) handler. Because React's autoFocus fires after the gesture has ended, iOS Safari/PWA focuses the field (caret shows) but the keyboard does not pop up, so a user opening search must tap the field a second time before they can type. Desktop Chrome/Firefox/Edge and Android Chrome are unaffected.
findings.fixSketch: Focus the input synchronously inside the same tap handler that opens the dialog (call ref.focus() in the open callback), rather than depending on autoFocus/effect-time focus.

findings.title: copyNoteLink calls navigator.clipboard.writeText unguarded with no execCommand fallback (inconsistent with clipboard.ts)
affectedClients: any client in an insecure context
findings.description: copyNoteLink calls `await navigator.clipboard.writeText(window.location.href)` directly. `navigator.clipboard` is undefined outside a secure context (http:// origins, common for self-hosted LAN deployments). Everywhere else the app routes copying through clipboard.ts:3 which guards `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` and falls back to a textarea + execCommand. copyNoteLink bypasses that helper.
findings.why: In an insecure context `navigator.clipboard` is undefined so `.writeText` throws; the try/catch swallows it and the 'copy note link' action silently does nothing with no fallback. Self-hosters running Hatchdoor over plain HTTP on a LAN (a realistic deployment for this app) get a dead button. Secure HTTPS launches are unaffected.
findings.fixSketch: Route copyNoteLink through the existing copyText() helper in clipboard.ts so it gets the `?.` guard and the execCommand fallback, and surface a failure notice instead of silently swallowing.

findings.title: Folder autocomplete uses <datalist>, which degrades on iOS/older WebKit
findings.description: The Create and Move forms drive folder suggestions with `<input list=...>` + `<datalist>` (FolderDatalist at lines 143-148; inputs at 179-186 and 263-270). datalist rendering is uneven on WebKit: iOS Safari historically had no dropdown UI and support remains inconsistent across iOS versions, and it is unstyleable.
findings.why: On affected iOS WebKit the datalist dropdown of existing folder paths simply does not appear, so the folder autocomplete affordance is silently missing. It is a graceful degradation (the field is still a plain text input the user can type into) rather than a break, hence low severity, but it is an uneven-support surface worth noting for the iPhone/iPad PWA target.
findings.fixSketch: If folder suggestions matter on mobile, replace the datalist with a custom filtered dropdown (the app already has an autocomplete pattern in autocomplete.ts), or accept the plain-input degradation explicitly.
